paper.citation: Zhou, X. (2022). Semiparametric estimation for causal mediation analysis with multiple causally ordered mediators. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology 84(3), 794-821. DOI: 10.1111/rssb.12487.
paper.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology
paper.source_locator: Section 5 'A Simulation Study' (arXiv:2011.12751v2 PDF page 28) gives the structural model; Supplementary Material F (arXiv:2011.12751v2 PDF page 56) gives the numerical coefficients beta_X1..beta_X4, beta_A, beta_M1, beta_M2, beta_Y. Estimand cPSE defined in Section 4.4 and equation (19), PDF page 32.

mechanism.name: Cumulative path-specific effect through the second of two causally ordered mediators

sampling.dependence: iid individuals; all variables within an individual are generated jointly in temporal order

assumptions: Consistency and well-defined joint interventions on A, M1 and M2
Pearl NPSEM with mutually independent errors, as assumed by the source (its Assumptions 1-3)
Causal ordering A -> M1 -> M2 -> Y with no M2 -> M1 arrow
Cross-world independence implied by the mutually independent-error NPSEM; cPSEs are not identified by conditional-exchangeability assumptions alone
Treatment positivity on the declared support; the logistic propensity is bounded away from 0 and 1 for finite covariates but no uniform overlap bound is claimed on unbounded Gaussian support
The latent variable UXY confounds X and Y but, as the source states, does not threaten identification of theta_{a1,a2,a3} because it is a pre-treatment common cause

properties.notes: Four baseline covariates X1..X4, all four of which enter the treatment, both mediator and the outcome equations with nonzero coefficients, so dimension = effective_dimension = 4. Not high dimensional: p = 4 against the source sample size n = 2000. No product/interaction term appears anywhere in the structural equations, hence interactions = false. nonlinear = true refers only to the logistic link in the treatment equation logit P(A=1|X) = (1,X1..X4) beta_A; the M1, M2 and Y conditional means are linear in their arguments. X1..X4 are mutually dependent because they share the latent errors U1,U2,U3,UXY.

estimand.name: cPSE_M2 = theta_011 - theta_001
estimand.definition: Cumulative path-specific effect through the second mediator: theta_{a1,a2,a3} = E[Y(a3, M1(a1), M2(a2, M1(a1)))], and cPSE_M2 = theta_011 - theta_001 holds the Y-argument at A=1 and the M1-argument at A=0 while moving only the M2-argument from A=0 to A=1. This is NOT the natural indirect effect, NOT the natural direct effect and NOT the total effect.

truth.expression: Cumulative path-specific effect through the second mediator: theta_{a1,a2,a3} = E[Y(a3, M1(a1), M2(a2, M1(a1)))], and cPSE_M2 = theta_011 - theta_001 holds the Y-argument at A=1 and the M1-argument at A=0 while moving only the M2-argument from A=0 to A=1. This is NOT the natural indirect effect, NOT the natural direct effect and NOT the total effect.
truth.derivation: Closed form. Because M1, M2 and Y are linear with additive mean-zero noise and A is intervened on, cPSE_M2 = beta_Y[M2] * beta_M2[A] = 0.96 * 0.34. The pre-treatment terms, the latent UXY and all X contributions cancel in the contrast.

adaptations: Version used: arXiv:2011.12751v2 (2021-11-10) preprint of the JRSS-B 2022 article; the journal version was not accessible to the collector, so section/page locators refer to the preprint PDF and the coefficient values are taken from its Supplementary Material F. Any numbering difference between preprint and journal version is unverified.

The source draws beta_X1..beta_X4 and beta_Y from Uniform[-1,1], beta_A from Uniform[-0.5,0.5], and beta_M1, beta_M2 from Uniform[0,0.5]; Supplementary Material F reports the realised values, which are registered here as FIXED parameters of one mechanism. The uniform draw itself is not re-sampled, so this is a single fixed mechanism, not a hyperdistribution.

Registered target is the cumulative path-specific effect cPSE_M2 = theta_011 - theta_001 that the source analyses in Section 5. The source reports no numerical value for it (its Figure 3 only re-centres estimators at the truth); the value 0.3264 registered here is derived analytically by the collector from the registered coefficients and must be checked by a reviewer.

The source generates 1000 Monte Carlo samples of size 2000 and compares eight estimators under five misspecification cases; none of that estimation work is reproduced. The 'false covariates' Z = (X1, exp(X2/2), (X3/X1)^(1/3), X4/(exp(X1/2)+1)) used there are an estimation device applied to the same data, not a different data-generating mechanism, so they are not registered as a separate DGP.
Sampling is re-implemented with NumPy Generator(PCG64); no attempt is made to match the source software draw-for-draw.
Only the eight observed columns are exported. The latent errors U1,U2,U3 and the latent X-Y confounder UXY are generated internally and never returned.
